- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive and price is consolidating; add 0.3–0.8% to forecast.
- If last 3–5 days show mean reversion (price moving back toward 30-day MA), model often misses it; adjust forecast to align with MA.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is strong or volatile.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for bearish bias.
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
